points.description: States that the algorithm is implemented, i.e. written as a program/code (or otherwise made runnable/executed). Equivalent wording such as 'code the algorithm', 'write a program for it', or 'run the algorithm' earns the mark.

States that the physical/actual running time is measured while the implemented algorithm executes, e.g. using a timer/clock to record elapsed time. Wording such as 'time how long it actually takes to run' earns full marks. Counting operations or giving only a theoretical complexity does not earn this point.

levels.says: Mentions measuring time/performance but does not make clear that the actual/physical running time of the implemented algorithm is measured (e.g. vague 'measure the time' with no execution context).

rubric.notes: Full marks require both implementing/running the algorithm and measuring its actual physical elapsed running time. Award part marks when only one of these components is present, or when the timing idea is too vague to show actual execution time. Purely theoretical operation counts or complexity analysis earn no marks for this experimental approach.
